newsitem.title: UK: GrandMet dismisses bid for BolsWessanen.
newsitem.headline: GrandMet dismisses bid for BolsWessanen.

text.p: British food and drinks group Grand Metropolitan dismissed on Tuesday as market speculation a report in Dutch daily newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad that it had launched a bid for Dutch group BolsWessanen.
"This is market speciulation. GrandMet has ruled big acquisitions off the agenda to concentrate on the organic growth of our brands," said a company spokesman.

GrandMet executives set out the company's strategy last week at the time of its full year results. Group finance director Gerald Corbett told Reuters then, "The message is -- steady as she goes, managing what we have got, building our brands and keeping the ship on a steady course."

The company ruled out any major acquisitions but said it would still look at small bolt on deals of around 50-60 million stg. BolsWessanen is valued at about 1.0 billion stg at its current share price of 31.70 guilders.

GrandMet is also close to completing a disposal programme in Europe aimed at selling off a range of small local food companies and enabling it to focus in Europe on its major international brands -- Pillsbury, Green Giant, Haagen-Dasz and Old El Paso. BolsWessanen was formed in January 1993 through a merger of drinks group Bols and food concern Wessanen in what was seen as a defensive move to keep the firms out of foreign hands.
Analysts however repeatedly criticised the new entity as they saw insufficient synergies.

The company currently has a return on equity of 18.65 percent compared to 20.66 percent for its Dutch rival CSM NV. It reported pretax profits of 247.07 million guilders in the year to December 31, 1995, down from 334.9 million in 1994.
